record.paper_title: Open Problems in K-Stability of Fano Varieties
record.context_brief: Reduction mod p and Frobenius volume
record.original_question: Let x in (X, Delta) be a klt singularity over characteristic 0, and for each sufficiently large prime p let x_p in (X_p, Delta_p) be its reduction modulo p. Is the characteristic-zero normalized volume always the limit of the positive-characteristic Frobenius volumes, namely vol^(x, X, Delta) = lim_{p -> infinity} Fvol(x_p, X_p, Delta_p)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a klt pair defined over a field of characteristic zero (say a finitely generated $\mathbb{Q}$-subalgebra $A\subset\mathbb{C}$), and let $x\in X$ be a closed point such that the germ $x\in(X,\Delta)$ is a klt singularity. Recall that the normalized volume function of Li is defined on the space $\mathrm{Val}_{X,x}$ of real valuations of the function field of $X$ centered at $x$ by
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{(X,\Delta),x}(v) \;=\; A_{(X,\Delta)}(v)^{n}\cdot\mathrm{vol}(v),$$
where $n=\dim X$, $A_{(X,\Delta)}(v)$ is the log discrepancy of $v$ with respect to $(X,\Delta)$, and $\mathrm{vol}(v)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\ell(\mathcal{O}_{X,x}/\mathfrak{a}_m(v))/(m^n/n!)$ is the volume of $v$. The normalized volume of the singularity is
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X,\Delta)\;=\;\inf_{v\in\mathrm{Val}_{X,x}}\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}_{(X,\Delta),x}(v).$$

For each sufficiently large prime $p$, choose a model of $(X,\Delta)$ over $\mathrm{Spec}\,A$ and let $x_p\in(X_p,\Delta_p)$ denote the reduction modulo $p$ of the singularity $x\in(X,\Delta)$ (so $X_p$ is a variety over a field of characteristic $p$). In characteristic $p>0$, the Frobenius-volume (or $F$-volume) of a klt singularity $y\in(Y,\Gamma)$ of dimension $n$ is defined via the Frobenius signature/F-signature-type invariant by
$$\mathrm{Fvol}(y,Y,\Gamma)\;=\;\inf_{\mathfrak{a}\,\mathfrak{m}\text{-primary}} \mathrm{lct}(Y,\Gamma;\mathfrak{a})^{n}\cdot e_{HK}(\mathfrak{a}),$$
or equivalently through the analogous Frobenius-theoretic local volume invariant, where $\mathrm{lct}$ is the log canonical threshold and $e_{HK}$ is the Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity (and one may equivalently use the $s$-invariant / F-signature formulation appropriate to klt pairs in characteristic $p$).

Question: does one always have
$$\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(x,X,\Delta)\;=\;\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathrm{Fvol}(x_p,X_p,\Delta_p)\;?$$
artifact.category_tag: K-stability and normalized volume of klt singularities
artifact.status_search_result: The equality between the characteristic-zero normalized volume and the limit of Frobenius volumes under reduction mod p is posed as Question 6.19 in the Li–Liu–Xu guided tour to normalized volume and is reiterated as an open problem in surveys on K-stability of Fano varieties. Available literature on normalized volume and on F-signature/Hilbert–Kunz invariants discusses partial inequalities and special cases but does not contain a proof of the full equality, and no resolution has been located.

status_evidence.title: A guided tour to normalized volume
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses normalized volume of klt singularities and poses questions relating it to positive-characteristic invariants under reduction mod p.
status_evidence.claim: The equality vol_hat = lim Fvol is stated as an open question in the LLX guided tour.

status_evidence.title: Stability of klt singularities (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys recent progress on normalized volume and K-stability of klt singularities, listing remaining open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys list the comparison with Frobenius volume as not yet established.
